newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - FEB 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - FEB 3.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--A new poll shows both ruling party PASOK and conservative opposition New Democracy failing to make the grade with voters on their handling of recent protests. Over 50 percent said the role of PASOK and ND in the protests were negative.

--Marathon negotiations with Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis have once again failed to reach a compromise although there are reports of light at the end of the tunnel. Primary school teachers will join high school teachers in their strike today and tomorrow.
--In Thessaloniki, the gala to officially inaugurate the city's tenure as Cultural Capital for 1997 went ahead amidst protests by 600 teachers.
--Checks on credit card spending have betrayed some 2000 stores which attempted to conceal some 15 billion drachmas in turnover. Cross-checking against this year's tax declarations will continue.
--ND deputy president Ioannis Varvitsiotis calls on president Miltiades Evert to clarify now whether he will stand for the leadership of the party at the forthcoming congress.

--There are changes afoot in the Greek military with Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos reportedly considering cutting national service by three months for those who join immediately on leaving high school.
--The state is losing 50 billion drachmas in tariffs per annum by the black market trade in pure alcohol smuggled into Greece from Italy.

--Farmers are gearing up for their last stand against an estimated 6,500 police forces deployed in the Thessaly area. Justice Minister Evangelos Venizelos said yesterday that farmers' leaders wanted bloodshed, while leader Yannos Patakis retorted that the government was the one wanting to draw blood.
